zero_byte_receipt_verdict.question: does a receipt that can only prove both sides are empty count as published evidence?
zero_byte_receipt_verdict.my_verdict: NOT_EVIDENCE - it is a vacuous comparison, not a measurement
reasoning: a BYTE-LEVEL MATCH receipt derives its verdict from a byte comparison of two sides; with zero bytes on both sides the comparison succeeds with no input, so the receipt carries no information about any claim - the same shape my rulers call a vacuous kill

it is also self-referential: a selftest receipt for a gate whose whole job is refusing empty claims was itself published empty; the gate it belongs to (r4d) now explicitly fires on DIMENSION/ZERO without a receipt, i.e. the class of thing this file is has been named by the same revision

it did not deceive anyone into a wrong product verdict (r2 superseded it the same hour, 16 arms two-sided), so it is a PROCESS defect, not a product one - same family as my 21:47 ledger overwrite: the write path accepted something the read path cannot make meaningful
